subject: MAP: reservation & evaluation runway for SlateAI capacity
messages:
From: Jade Lin <jade@slateai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial capacity ask + timeline (SlateAI)

Neha, Ben —

Thanks for taking the meeting earlier. Quick summary of where SlateAI landed after the product review: we expect to move a critical feature into beta that relies on a 70B LLM family (mix of Llama-3 variants and some proprietary finetunes). Target launch to limited customers in EU by Nov 15.

Sizing: rough peak estimate is ~1.2M tokens/day initially, with burst days up to 2.8M tokens. Latency target for the feature is <= 250ms p50.

Key asks:
- A concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lists evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and procurement checkpoints.
- Clear lead times for Dedicated vs Private (VPC) deployments — procurement window matters for our security/compliance team.
- Options for GPU pool sizing + hedging if we need to scale faster.

I've attached a short traffic estimate workbook for context (slate_traffic_estimate.xlsx). Procurement is looped on procurement@slateai.com — they will need tentative contract terms and any expected commit cadence.

Can you send an initial MAP draft today or tomorrow? We want to align internal stakeholders.

— Jade
Jade Lin
Head of Platform
SlateAI
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jade Lin <jade@slateai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-20T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask + timeline (SlateAI)

Jade — thanks for the clear brief and the workbook, that helps. I put together a compact MAP draft below (attached as redwood_map_draft_v1.docx). High-level approach and assumptions first, then a recommended schedule that matches your Nov 15 target.

Assumptions:
- Primary model family: Llama-3 70B quantized to int8 for latency/cost tradeoff.
- Region: EU (we'll plan for AWS eu-west-1 / GCP europe-west).
- Acceptance criteria: p50 latency <= 250ms on standard prompt set; throughput validated at 2.8M tokens/day burst profile; fidelity regression <= 3% on your eval set.

Proposed MAP (milestones & owners):
1) Eval sprint (2 weeks) — slate test prompts + Redwood perf harness. Owner: Neha. Deliverable: perf baseline, cost/latency profile. Target: 2025-09-05.
2) Integration & security review (3 weeks parallel to perf tuning) — Owner: Slate security + Redwood security engineer. Deliverable: checklist completion (networking, KMS, audit logs). Target: 2025-09-26.
3) Capacity commit decision (mutual sign) — choose Dedicated reserve or Private deployment. Owner: Slate procurement + Ben for pricing. Target: 2025-10-03.
4) Procurement & procurement onboarding (4–6 weeks) — contract, billing, SOC2 evidence if needed. Owner: procurement@slateai.com + Redwood sales ops. Target: 2025-11-07.
5) Staged rollout & acceptance (2 weeks) — owner: Tessa (onboarding). Go-live: target 2025-11-15.

Lead-time guidance (Dedicated vs Private):
- Dedicated (hosted reserved GPU pool): typical commit-to-availability lead time ~ 2–4 weeks after signed agreement depending on tranche (we size for burst buckets).
- Private (VPC or on-prem): typical lead time 6–10 weeks (networking, KMS setup, HSM/KMS onboarding adds time).

GPU pool sizing recommendations (based on your burst profile):
- Minimum: 4 x H100 80GB configured for mixed-precision (int8) — supports baseline throughput but low headroom.
- Recommended hedge (preferred): 8 x H100 80GB with autoscaling tranches to reach 12 x H100 during expected bursts. This gives headroom for 2.8M token burst days with latency buffer and rolling maintenance.
- Alternative (cost-sensitive): 12 x A100 40GB with tighter batching; higher tail latency risk on long prompts.

Hedging strategy: commit to a baseline reserved tranche (4 H100) + option to add burst tranches billed at a higher burst rate. This reduces initial commit while providing runway for spikes.

Next steps: confirm whether Slate will pursue Dedicated or Private for this engagement (we can run the eval on Hosted and then port to Private later if needed). If you confirm, I'll circulate a v2 MAP with explicit acceptance tests and a DocuSign link for the commitment tranche.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales, Capacity & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_map_draft_v1.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jade Lin <jade@slateai.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-21T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask + timeline (SlateAI) — pricing & SLA note

Quick follow-up on pricing mechanics for the MAP:
- Baseline reserved tranche (4 H100) — example monthly commit: $X/month (I gave a range in the attached doc).
- Burst tranches — billed on an elevated on-demand rate but capped per month as part of the agreed tranche policy.
- SLA: we can offer a 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated; Private deployments can be SLA-backed depending on support tier.

Tessa, I'll sync with you on acceptance-runbook details once Neha finalizes the MAP v2.

— Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Jade Lin <jade@slateai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@slateai.com
Date: 2025-08-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask + timeline (SlateAI)

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- We prefer Dedicated to start (faster to provision for our immediate beta) but we need the option to move to Private within 3 months (security review scheduled).
- EU region is mandatory for data residency.
- Acceptance tests: we'll provide a short eval set (redacted) — need to verify fidelity/regression metrics.

Procurement is asking for an explicit commit window and whether Redwood can accommodate shorter lead time for Dedicated if we accept price escalation for burst tranches. Also, can you indicate whether Redwood will pre-provision a warm standby tranche for faster cutover?

Procurement contact (for the contract): procurement@slateai.com

Jade
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jade Lin <jade@slateai.com>, procurement@slateai.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-24T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask + timeline (SlateAI) — MAP v2 and commit runway

Jade / Procurement —

Attached is MAP v2 (redwood_map_v2.pdf) with explicit acceptance test cases, a commit runway table, and a proposed DocuSign for the baseline tranche. Key updates:
- We can pre-warm a standby tranche (4 H100) for an additional short-term fee; this reduces commit-to-availability to ~3–5 business days for Dedicated.
- Private remains 6–10 weeks depending on network onboarding and KMS/HSM timelines.
- Commit runway table included: baseline (4 H100) -> add-on tranche (4 H100) -> peak (12 H100). Pricing tiers and on-demand caps are listed.

Action items I need from Slate:
1) Confirm Dedicated baseline acceptance and whether you want pre-warm standby.
2) Procurement: confirm signatory and preferred contract cadence so I can generate DocuSign.
3) Security: share eval prompts and any SOC2 controls to validate (we'll collate evidence).

If Slate confirms baseline by 2025-10-03, we can hit the Nov 15 go-live target under the proposed MAP.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales, Capacity & Onboarding
Redwood Inference
